title: Resolve the dangling 'pacified' exclusion that disables the modifier conflict rule
body:
## Summary
The only elite-modifier exclusion in the roster points at a modifier id that does not exist, so the exclusion UI in four call sites never fires.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts:302 declares Enraged `excludes: ['pacified']`; no ELITE_MODIFIERS entry has id 'pacified' (repo-wide grep: 1 hit, the declaration). The exclusion logic in src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:83, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ArchetypeBuilder.tsx:22,79 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ExpandedDetails.tsx:60 is therefore dead code in practice. data.ts belongs to the sibling context bestiary-encounters-metrics, so this round could not edit it. Fixed = the id resolves to a real opposing modifier (or the entry is removed) and a test pins that every excludes id resolves and the relation is symmetric.

## Flow
- open Archetypes, expand a card, activate Enraged
- no modifier greys out: the excluded id matches nothing
- fix: add/repair the target modifier, add a resolves-and-symmetric test over ELITE_MODIFIERS

## Expected impact
Designers get the conflict rule the UI was built for; measured by the resolves test. Risk: adding a modifier changes generated GE code for that modifier only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the modifier exclusion rule actually applies
Before: 1 of 1 excludes ids dangling (0 resolvable)
After: predicted 0 dangling; not run - file is sibling-owned
Method: simulation - grep over ELITE_MODIFIERS ids; edit out of this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/_shared/data.ts:302  geClass: 'GE_Elite_Enraged', excludes: ['pacified'],
grep -rn pacified src -> 1 hit (the line above)
instrument: vitest: every ELITE_MODIFIERS[].excludes id resolves to a modifier and the relation is symmetric (seed: current data -> red)

title: Extract the elite-modifier exclusion rule duplicated in four sites
body:
## Summary
The toggle-with-exclusion reducer and the is-excluded predicate are each hand-written twice.

## Description
Toggle reducer: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:76-87 (toggleCardModifier) and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ArchetypeBuilder.tsx:18-25 (toggleBuilderModifier). Predicate: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ExpandedDetails.tsx:60 and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ArchetypeBuilder.tsx:79. Both copies are one-directional (they consult only the newly added mod's excludes), so an asymmetric pair can co-exist from one side. Fixed = one pure helper (toggleModifier / isModifierExcluded) consumed by all four sites, with a test covering an asymmetric fixture.

## Flow
- add a pure helper beside elite-stat-axes in src/lib/bestiary/
- replace the 4 sites
- test with an asymmetric excludes fixture

## Expected impact
One rule instead of four; the dangling-id card becomes a one-line data fix. Risk: index.tsx is the shell; behaviour must stay identical for current data.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the exclusion rule
Before: 4 sites (2 reducers, 2 predicates)
After: predicted 1 helper + 4 call sites
Method: simulation - site count by grep; helper not built (touches shell + 2 components, M)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: unit test of the helper with asymmetric fixture {a.excludes:[b]}: adding b while a is active must drop a (fails on both current copies)

title: Reset archetype pagination on any filter change, not only a count change
body:
## Summary
The page index resets only when the filtered COUNT changes, so a filter switch yielding the same count keeps the user on page N of a different set.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ArchetypesTab.tsx:253-258 tracks prevFilterLen and resets page only when filteredArchetypes.length differs. Two role/area filters with equal result counts leave the user mid-list in an unrelated result set. Fixed = key the reset on the filter tuple (search, role, category, tier, area).

## Flow
- go to page 3 with role=melee
- switch to a role with the same match count
- page stays 3; expected page 1

## Expected impact
Designers filtering the 94-entry roster always land on the first page of a new result. Risk: low; one render-phase reset.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - filter change always shows page 1
Before: reset only on length change (code read)
After: predicted reset on every filter change
Method: simulation - needs two filters with equal counts over 94 archetypes and >24 matches; not probed this round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: component test: find two filter values with equal counts > PAGE_SIZE, go to page 2, switch filter, assert "Page 1 /"

title: Complete the behaviour-tree keyboard model (Home/End, parent/child arrows)
body:
## Summary
The BT tree has roving focus now but lacks the rest of the tree keyboard model: Home/End, ArrowLeft to parent, ArrowRight into first child.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/ai-logic/BTFlowchart.tsx:100-139 handles Up/Down, and Left/Right only toggle collapse. Registry accessibility / keyboard-navigation-models (arrows within composites, Home/End jump to edges) and the WAI tree pattern expect ArrowLeft on an expanded-or-leaf child to move to its parent and ArrowRight on an expanded node to move to its first child. With 54 nodes / 15 parents, reaching a parent from a deep leaf costs repeated ArrowUp.

## Flow
- focus a depth-3 leaf
- press ArrowLeft: nothing happens (expected: parent focused)
- press Home: nothing (expected: root)

## Expected impact
Keyboard users traverse the tree in O(depth) not O(rows). Risk: key handler only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - keyboard tree traversal cost
Before: 0 of 4 keys (Home, End, Left-to-parent, Right-to-child) implemented
After: predicted 4 of 4
Method: simulation - read the switch; parent map not yet built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: keyboard test in bt-flowchart-roving-focus.test.tsx: Home/End/Left/Right focus targets

title: Fix or implement the 'compared enemies auto-added' radar claim
body:
## Summary
The shell comment says compared enemies are auto-added to the radar overlays; toggleCompare never touches radarOverlays.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:64 comment: "only player enabled by default; compared enemies auto-added". toggleCompare (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:55-62) updates compareIds only; radarOverlays changes only via toggleOverlay (:89-91). Either implement the auto-add (a capability inside the declared radar-comparison scope) or correct the comment.

## Flow
- add 2 enemies to comparison
- radar shows only the player
- decide: implement auto-add (test) or correct the comment (XS)

## Expected impact
A maintainer stops trusting a false invariant; if implemented, the radar follows the comparison. Risk: none for the comment; auto-add may surprise users who toggled overlays off.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - comment matches behaviour
Before: 1 false claim (code read)
After: 0
Method: simulation - behaviour read; product choice between two fixes
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:64  /* Radar overlay toggles — only player enabled by default; compared enemies auto-added */
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/index.tsx:55-62 toggleCompare: setCompareIds only
instrument: component test: compare 2 enemies -> assert overlay checkboxes for both are checked (if implementing), else comment edit

title: Re-home AggroTable and ArchetypeBuilder in the context that renders them
body:
## Summary
Two files mapped to bestiary-archetypes-ai are consumed only by the encounters tab of a sibling context.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/ai-logic/AggroTable.tsx and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/archetypes/ArchetypeBuilder.tsx are listed in this context's file_paths, but their only renderer is src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersTab.tsx (grep: AggroTable 1 consumer, ArchetypeBuilder 1 consumer + 1 test). Ownership and folder disagree with use, so a sweep of one context edits UI another context ships. Fixed = context-map update (and optionally a folder move).

## Flow
- grep consumers
- operator/director decides: move the files under encounters/ or re-map them in context-map.json

## Expected impact
Parallel sweeps stop overlapping on encounters UI. Risk: import path churn if moved.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - context ownership matches usage
Before: 2 files mapped here, rendered only by a sibling context
After: 0 after re-map
Method: probe - consumer grep
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
grep -rln AggroTable src -> src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersTab.tsx
grep -rln ArchetypeBuilder src -> src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/encounters/EncountersTab.tsx, src/__tests__/components/bestiary-focus-ring.test.tsx

title: Wave Spawner Configurator shows hard-coded numbers as if configured
body:
## Summary
The AI Logic tab's spawner panel prints '60s / 12 / 800cm' from an inline literal, not from any spawn config.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/ai-logic/AILogicTab.tsx:87 renders [{Wave Inter 60s},{Max Active 12},{Spawn Radius 800cm}] inline, under a status badge driven by the real 'Spawn system' feature row. A designer reads them as the project's values. Recorded deviation covers DecisionDebugger only (agent-behaviour-authoring). Fixed = source from a real spawn config / the UE project, or label the block as an example.

## Flow
- open AI Logic, expand Wave Spawner Configurator
- values never change with project or enemy
- decide: wire to real config (direction) or label as example

## Expected impact
Designers stop acting on numbers nobody configured. Risk: none for labelling.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - displayed config is real or marked as example
Before: 3 of 3 values literal
After: depends on direction chosen
Method: probe - source read
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_bestiary/ai-logic/AILogicTab.tsx:87  {[{ label: 'Wave Inter', value: '60s' }, { label: 'Max Active', value: '12' }, { label: 'Spawn Radius', value: '800cm' }]
